canonical_definition:
What it is. Most commonly, papers treat it as a continual learning benchmark built from classification datasets. One description presents the standard CL benchmarks as having 4 tasks and 5 categories for assessing performance across task sequences, while another presents a benchmark for language models made up of five text classification datasets: AG News, Amazon Reviews, Yelp Reviews, DBpedia, and Yahoo Answers.

What it is claimed to measure. The recorded measurement use is concentrated on text classification. Papers link it to one behavioral indicator, text classification, describing it as five text classification datasets or five text classification tasks, and no constructs are linked to it.

Space of uses. Papers use it as an evaluation benchmark in continual learning, including for assessing model performance across task sequences and for evaluation setups described as designed for language models. No other measurement instrument is linked to it.

Recurrent Knowledge Identification and Fusion for Language Model Continual Learning
